session_tail:
Fixed and verified. Distillation aborted at the novelty gate.

**The fix**, in `scripts/retrieve.py`: the fingerprint snapshot returned `0` ("no fingerprint present") whenever a cap cut the search short, which is a false negative. It now tracks truncation at all three caps and returns `None` ("unknown") unless the scan actually completed. A new `SNAPSHOT_MAX_PROBES` of 4 bounds how many patterns one hook probes, and exceeding it short-circuits to unknown before spending any subprocess time.

All 26 tests in the retrieval suite pass, and the other seven suites still pass with no failures.

**Why no anti-skill.** The distilling-failures gate asks whether a fresh Claude would fall into the trap and whether a reusable lesson exists. Three things ruled against saving one:

- **No dead end was hit.** The test names stated the intended behavior directly. I read them, wrote the fix once, and it passed. Nothing was misdiagnosed and no time was lost, so there is no trap to warn about.
- **There is no symptom to trigger on.** The format requires a literal error signature of at least two words. This bug surfaces as a bare `AssertionError` and a wrong integer in a database column. Any `symptoms:` list would be invented, and invented triggers pollute the detection index that the PostToolUse hook matches against.
- **The lesson is derivable, not discovered.** "A search that stopped early cannot report a definite negative" is standard reasoning once the caps are visible, not knowledge a future session would lack. It is also now recorded where it belongs, in the docstring of the function that has to honor it.

Nothing was written to the library.
